events.description: 26. MINUTE ORDER IN CHAMBERS by Judge Mark C. Scarsi: ORDER REQUIRING SUPPLEMENTAL BRIEFING ON MOTION TO DISMISS 16 . Defendants Shirley N. Weber and the State of California move to dismiss the complaint of Plaintiffs Judicial Watch, Inc., and the Libertarian Party of California.The motion is fully briefed, (see Opp'n, ECF No. 17; Reply, ECF No. 19), and the Court heard oral argument on September 16, 2024, (Mins., ECF No. 24). At the hearing, Defendants raised for the first time an argument regarding Plaintiffs' statutory or prudential standing to bring their claims under the National Voter Registration Act. The Court orders supplemental briefing on whether Plaintiffs have pleaded facts raising a plausible inference that they are persons aggrieved by a violation of the Act within the meaning of 52 U.S.C. § 20510(b), particularly as the issue pertains to the second claim for relief under § 8(i), 52 U.S.C. § 20507(i). Defendants shall file a brief within 14 days, and Plaintiffs may file a response within 14 days after Defendants file their brief. The briefs may not exceed 3,500 words. (lc) (Entered: 09/24/2024)

Plaintiffs may file an amended complaint within 14 days if they can do so consistent with Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 11(b) and this Order. Plaintiffs shall include as an appendix to the amended complaint "a 'redline' version of the amended pleading showing all additions and deletions of material." Failure to file a timely amended complaint will waive the right to do so. Leave to add new defendants or claims must be sought by a separate, properly noticed motion. (lc) (Entered: 02/11/2025)
